chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Aamir ibn Abdullah ibn Juza'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no servant who recites the end of Surah Al-Kahf except that he will wake up in the hour that he intends.

key_terms.تَيَقَّظَ: He will wake up / become alert

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of reciting the end of Surah Al-Kahf?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the spiritual potency of concluding one's Quranic recitation with Surah Al-Kahf, linking it to divine facilitation of wakefulness (tayaqudh) at a chosen hour. Scholars interpret this 'wakefulness' not merely as physical alertness but as a state of spiritual vigilance and readiness for divine encounter, often associated with the time of Fajr or the Hour of Death. This practice is viewed as a means of securing Allah's help in maintaining consciousness of the Divine during critical moments of transition.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Aban, from Aamir Bin Abdullah Bin Juza’at,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is none from a servant who recites the end of (Surah) Al-Kahf except he will wake up in the time which he intended to’.
en.sarwar: 21. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Aban from ‘Amir ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Jadha’h from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever reads the last verse of al-Kahf (Chapter 18) can wake up at night at the hour that he intends to wake up.”
